Save → prepare → use. Saving puts a file on storage. Packages still need installation, archives need extraction and payloads need a compatible loader. Set up the local downloader to choose console folders; a stock console browser cannot write to arbitrary paths.

Save apps, menus & payload files

The console downloader uses the installed ezRemote background service to save files to internal storage or a mounted USB drive.

Set up console downloader Open console downloader

Create folders & extract archives

Open the running ezRemote client, then explicitly create or verify the whatwhatboy download folder. Saved, reviewed archives up to 32 MiB can be checksum-checked and extracted into a new folder through their archive cards.

Open folder preparation

Choose files for your console

Save on console opens your installed local downloader. It does not start a transfer until you select Save to console there.

PS4 ELF engine. Project-confirmed firmware range 9.00–12.52; requires a compatible elfldr listening on 9021. The ELF is not a BIN payload.

Start the compatible PS4 elfldr and explicitly send the Orbis ELF to port 9021. Then open the patch manager on console port 23900; use /data/user/patches/xml_orbis for CUSA XML files.

Browse and install with a native app

Add this source in PS4 Games Installer → Options → Settings → Games JSON URL, test the connection and save. Browse and install the listed homebrew packages in the app. Its r40 documentation tests PS4 11.00 with GoldHEN; this does not establish PS4 14.00 support.

Get PS4 Games Installer Catalogue instructions

Set up the console downloader once

  1. Prepare homebrew and ezRemoteUse a working homebrew environment and install ezRemote Client 2.08 for PS4. Use a GoldHEN setup supported by the app. Enable its BIN Loader when starting ezRemote Server. This is a one-time prerequisite for the downloader.
  2. Save the companion page on this consoleIn ezRemote, use its direct-link download feature to save the HTML URL below as /data/whatsite-ps4.html. Use the existing /data folder.
  3. Start the matching servicesEnable background downloads in ezRemote settings and start its bundled ezRemote Server on port 6701. Keep ezRemote Client running with its web service available on port 8080 for folder creation and extraction. The client’s port 8080 file manager is separate from the background server. Keep the console awake during an operation.
  4. Open the console downloaderOpen http://127.0.0.1:6701/data/whatsite-ps4.html in the console’s browser. The local page can talk to the download service and show its transfer queue.
  5. Choose storage and prepare its download folderInternal storage defaults to /data/whatwhatboy. For USB storage, inspect the actual mounted path in ezRemote and enter its whatwhatboy download folder. Choose Prepare download folder, then press Create or verify download folder on the client page. It creates only missing child folders, preserves existing directories and refuses colliding files. Choose Use this verified folder in the downloader to return.
  6. Choose and save the compatible fileConfirm that the selected folder is writable and has enough space, then tick its confirmation in the downloader. Ready files are shown first. Press Save to console for the selected file and wait for the receiver’s reported completion. Packages still need installation; payloads need a compatible loader; plugins, patches and scripts need their exact game/update guide and any supporting files.
Get ezRemote 2.08 ezRemote installation instructions Open installed downloader Open folder preparation

The local address opens the PlayStation you are browsing on. From a phone or computer, enter that console’s LAN address above and enable the client’s web access if needed. These quick links use the documented default ports: 8080 for client folder actions and 6701 for background downloads. If you configured another client port, use its native file manager. PS4 and PS5 use different companion paths and protocols.

Choose storage that your console exposes

DestinationHow to choose it
Internal HDD / SSDThe default download folder is /data/whatwhatboy. Use Prepare download folder and explicitly create or verify it before saving. This stages a file; it does not select an installed game’s storage.
USB HDD / SSD / flash driveOpen ezRemote, confirm the actual mounted path, then prepare its whatwhatboy folder through the local client page. The pinned PS4 service cannot automatically enumerate USB mounts. Mount numbers do not identify a physical front or rear USB port.
PlayStation Extended StorageSystem-managed game storage is separate from general-purpose USB files. An external drive is usable here only if the homebrew service exposes a writable file folder.

Keep space for the file and its extracted or installed copy. A queued request is not a completed save; confirm the finished file in ezRemote. Match firmware, title ID and game update before installing or loading anything.

Extract a saved archive when needed

Choose Archives & complete packs to find the retained ZIP, RAR and 7z downloads. Save the complete archive first. In the local downloader, choose Extract a saved copy on console on its card, then press the explicit verification-and-extraction action on the client page.

Automatic extraction accepts reviewed archives up to 32 MiB only after checking the saved file’s SHA-256. It uses a new output folder and preserves the original archive. Other archives remain available through the real ezRemote file manager. Extraction shows an in-progress state and the native service’s result; the API does not supply a percentage. Nothing extracts, installs or launches when a page opens.
